race_context: The Metropolitan School District of Warren Township serves about 11,500 students on Indianapolis' far east side {cb_warren_guide}. In 2025-26 it ran one high school, three intermediate-middle schools (grades 5-8) and nine elementary schools {mi_fifth_delay} {mi_fifth_2025}. In 2023-24, about 55% of students were Black, about 20% were Hispanic, and almost 70% came from low-income backgrounds {cb_warren_2024}. Tim Hanson was identified as superintendent in 2023 coverage, and Mirror Indy quoted Hanson addressing the board in February 2026 {indystar_ref_2023} {mi_fifth_delay}.
The board has seven members, all elected at large to overlapping four-year terms; voters may vote for candidates for every open seat {cb_warren_2022} {cb_warren_guide}.

Three at-large seats are on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot, and winners serve January 2027 through December 2030 {cb_warren_guide}. The state list shows "vote for 1," which does not match the three open seats {in_list}.

The three seats now belong to board president Terri Amos, Rachel Burke and vice president Kevin Humphrey Sr., and all three are running again. Six candidates are running in all: the three incumbents and challengers Jerry Crites, Samantha Douglas and Steve Tutsie {cb_warren_guide}. Tutsie is listed as an Independent; the other five did not declare a party {cb_warren_guide} {in_list}.

Fifth-grade move: in September 2025, administrators proposed moving fifth graders from the intermediate-middle schools back into the elementary schools for fall 2026 {mi_fifth_2025}. The board approved the plan Feb. 4, 2026, but delayed it to 2027-28 because elementary schools would be over capacity without additions. The plan adds four classrooms each at Lowell, Pleasant Run, Hawthorne and Grassy Creek elementaries for about $21 million, paid with bonds rather than a tax-increase request. Some elementary school assignments may change {mi_fifth_delay}. Candidates who answered the 2026 survey said they support the change {cb_warren_guide}.

Referendum and budget: Warren voters approved an eight-year, $88 million operating referendum in 2023 for transportation, technology, academic programs, safety and staff wages {cb_warren_2024} {indystar_ref_2023}. The board's referendum spending plans total about $14.0 million for FY2026 (adopted March 19, 2025) and about $13.7 million for FY2027 (adopted March 24, 2026). In the FY2027 plan, the staff retention and support-staff line falls from $4.6 million to $3.5 million, and transportation rises from $3.3 million to about $4.5 million {warren_fy26_plan} {warren_fy27_plan}. Incumbents Amos and Humphrey named state funding and budget cuts as the most pressing issue {cb_warren_guide}.
Career education: Warren is using a $30 million Lilly Endowment grant to build career classrooms at every middle school, according to an associate superintendent {cb_lilly}.

Academics: in 2022, Warren had the lowest share of students passing both ILEARN math and English among Marion County districts (8%) {cb_warren_2022}. Third-grade IREAD results rose nearly 12 percentage points in spring 2024 {cb_warren_2024}, and in 2026 board president Amos said more than 83% of third graders passed and that the district is now focused on ILEARN math {cb_warren_guide}.

Forums and differences: no 2026 candidate forum was found. Five of six candidates answered the Chalkbeat Indiana/Mirror Indy/WFYI survey; Burke did not respond {cb_warren_guide}. The incumbents who answered pointed to state funding and budget cuts as the main challenge. Crites put feeding programs and a facilities review first, Douglas stressed keeping Warren families' first choice and community partnerships, and Tutsie focused on keeping and attracting middle school students {cb_warren_guide}.

candidates.summary: First-time candidate and retired Warren Township schools facilities director, running without a party label {cb_warren_guide} {in_list}.
background: Retired facilities director for Warren Township schools {cb_warren_guide}.
Does not have students now enrolled in the district; age 62 {cb_warren_guide}.
path_to_ballot: Listed on the state candidate list as Nonpartisan {in_list}.

items: Wants to raise test scores through targeted instruction, tutoring and intervention, and clear progress monitoring {cb_warren_guide}.
Said the district should focus on technology and digital literacy, including coding, data literacy and responsible use of AI, "not just access to devices" {cb_warren_guide}.

Named federal cutbacks to feeding programs as the most pressing issue; would protect those programs in the district budget, partner with food banks and nonprofits, and lobby state and federal officials {cb_warren_guide}.
Would work with the board and chief financial officer to review spending, find efficiencies and stay accountable to taxpayers {cb_warren_guide}.
Supports competitive salaries and incentives for both certified and classified staff {cb_warren_guide}.
Wants a thorough facility review that ranks repairs, safety upgrades and learning-space improvements by need {cb_warren_guide}.
For the fifth-grade move, would meet regularly with district officials to track construction progress and timelines {cb_warren_guide}.
Would respond directly to people who attend board meetings and make his contact information available on the district website {cb_warren_guide}.

on_incumbent: Did not criticize specific board decisions in his survey; he said elementary schools need an evaluation of space and capacity before the fifth-grade move {cb_warren_guide}.
plans: Wants to conduct a facilities evaluation and track renovation schedules for the fifth-grade transition {cb_warren_guide}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or campaign finance figures were found in reviewed sources {cb_warren_guide}.
gaps: No campaign website or social media page was found.
Marion County Election Board campaign finance filings were not reviewed; fundraising is unknown.
No news coverage beyond the Chalkbeat/Mirror Indy/WFYI survey was found.

candidates.summary: Incumbent and board vice president, first elected in 2022; a Marine Corps veteran and retired postal worker running without a party label {cb_warren_guide} {in_list}.
background: Served in the U.S. Marine Corps and is a retired postal worker {cb_warren_guide}.
Longtime youth sports volunteer; age 64 {cb_warren_guide}. In 2022 WFYI reported he had teaching experience and coached youth football {cb_warren_2022}.
First elected in 2022 and sworn in January 2023; now board vice president {cb_warren_guide} {indystar_ref_2023}.
path_to_ballot: Listed on the state candidate list as Nonpartisan {in_list}.

items: Named "the new budget cuts" as the most pressing issue and said the board "must work with legislators to reevaluate things" {cb_warren_guide}.
Said his approach to finances is "to stay fiscally disciplined" {cb_warren_guide}.
Named continued academic growth as a priority; said state policy and regulation changes "keep moving the goal post" {cb_warren_guide}.
Named increasing teacher salaries as a priority {cb_warren_guide}.
Named increasing enrollment (average daily membership) as a priority {cb_warren_guide}.
Said space is being added for the fifth-grade move and that the board will give teachers who change buildings "all the support they need" {cb_warren_guide}.

on_incumbent: Is a current board member and vice president. He supports the board-approved fifth-grade transition and described the space additions under way {cb_warren_guide} {mi_fifth_delay}.
plans: Wants to work with state legislators on school funding, raise teacher pay and grow enrollment {cb_warren_guide}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or campaign finance figures were found in reviewed sources {cb_warren_guide}.
gaps: No campaign website or social media page was found; his survey answers were brief.
No record of his individual board votes was reviewed.
Marion County Election Board campaign finance filings were not reviewed; fundraising is unknown.

candidates.summary: Incumbent and former board president seeking a fourth term, running without a party label; she was elected in June 2026 as the National PTA's vice president of advocacy {cb_warren_guide} {in_list}.
background: Born and raised in Warren Township and attended district schools including Warren Central {cb_warren_guide} {burke_site}.
Parent of three children who have attended district schools; has volunteered with robotics and Science Olympiad teams and parent-teacher groups {cb_warren_guide}.
Has served as board secretary, vice president and president {cb_warren_guide}. In 2022 WFYI reported she had served two non-consecutive terms and was president of the Indiana PTA {cb_warren_2022}.
Elected National PTA vice president of advocacy in June 2026 {cb_warren_guide}.
path_to_ballot: Listed on the state candidate list as Nonpartisan {in_list}.

items: In 2022, said she wanted to prioritize educational equity by meeting the needs of all students, especially those who fell behind during the pandemic {cb_warren_2022}.

Her campaign website, last updated in 2016-2018, lists "rebuilding and sustaining infrastructure" and public education as "the cornerstone of a productive democracy" among her issues {burke_site_issues}.

on_incumbent: Is a current board member and former president. She did not respond to the 2026 survey, so no 2026 account of the board's record from her was found {cb_warren_guide}.
plans: No 2026 plans were found; she did not respond to multiple requests to complete the Chalkbeat/Mirror Indy/WFYI survey {cb_warren_guide}.
endorsements_finance: Her campaign website's issues page, created in 2016, says she was endorsed by the Indiana State AFL-CIO; no 2026 endorsement was confirmed {burke_site_issues}.
gaps: Her campaign website appears to date from 2016-2018 (page dates in the site's public data) and may not reflect her 2026 positions.
Her website lists "MSD Warren Township Board of Trustees 2013-2016"; her exact service dates were not confirmed in news sources.
No record of her board votes was reviewed.
Marion County Election Board campaign finance filings were not reviewed; fundraising is unknown.

candidates.summary: First-time candidate, president of the Far Eastside Community Council and a Warren parent, running without a party label {cb_warren_guide} {in_list}.
background: President of the Far Eastside Community Council {cb_warren_guide}. Her campaign site says she is also Community Builder for the Far Eastside Quality of Life Plan, a communications professional, and host of The Black Briefing Podcast {douglas_site}.
Parent of students at Brookview Elementary, Stonybrook Intermediate and Middle School and Warren Central; a Warren graduate; age 36 {cb_warren_guide} {douglas_site}.
path_to_ballot: Listed on the state candidate list as Nonpartisan {in_list}.

items: Called keeping Warren "the first choice for families" the most pressing issue, and said the district should focus on being innovative, supportive and connected rather than "competing out of fear" {cb_warren_guide}.
Wants strong literacy and math instruction alongside investment in STEM, the arts, and career and technical education {cb_warren_guide}.

Said every financial decision should start with how it improves student outcomes, and that "we can't simply cut our way to excellence"; supports partnerships that expand opportunities without burdening families {cb_warren_guide}.
Wants to make decisions "with the community, not just for the community," and to give residents information on issues before the board {cb_warren_guide}.
Wants more communication with families and fewer barriers to family engagement {douglas_site}.

on_incumbent: Supports the board-approved fifth-grade transition and said she would ask questions and seek accountability during implementation {cb_warren_guide}.
plans: Wants to build partnerships among schools, families, nonprofits, businesses and neighborhood groups so schools serve as community hubs {cb_warren_guide} {douglas_site}.
endorsements_finance: Her campaign website takes online donations and volunteer sign-ups; no amounts raised or endorsements were found {douglas_site}.
gaps: Marion County Election Board campaign finance filings were not reviewed; fundraising is unknown.
No news coverage beyond the Chalkbeat/Mirror Indy/WFYI survey was found.

candidates.summary: First-time candidate running as an Independent; an assistant head football coach at Marian University who previously coached at Warren Central {cb_warren_guide} {in_list}.
background: Assistant head football coach at Marian University; held multiple coaching stints at Warren Central, including the 2006 state championship team {cb_warren_guide}.
Cites 12 years of service in Warren Township schools and experience as an educator at elementary, middle and high school levels {cb_warren_guide}.
Has no family now attending Warren schools; age 60 {cb_warren_guide}.
path_to_ballot: Listed on the state candidate list as an Independent; the ballot name includes the nickname "Coach" {in_list}.

items: Named keeping and attracting middle school students as the most pressing issue; called the fifth-grade move "one vital strategy" and wants paths for student success explored {cb_warren_guide}.

Wants elementary reading and math gains to continue, better identification of each middle schooler's academic and extracurricular needs, and a high school focus on the new state graduation requirements {cb_warren_guide}.
Said the board "must be responsible stewards of taxpayers' dollars with accountability" {cb_warren_guide}.
Plans to attend as many school activities as possible and encourage feedback {cb_warren_guide}.

on_incumbent: Supports the fifth-grade move; said the district should engage the affected teachers, parents and students to anticipate problems early {cb_warren_guide}.
plans: Wants a middle school retention strategy built on the fifth-grade move and on identifying individual student needs {cb_warren_guide}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or campaign finance figures were found in reviewed sources {cb_warren_guide}.
gaps: His Facebook page could not be reviewed; positions come only from the Chalkbeat/Mirror Indy/WFYI survey.
Marion County Election Board campaign finance filings were not reviewed; fundraising is unknown.

candidates.summary: Incumbent and board president, first elected in 2014, seeking a fourth term without a party label; she teaches in another school district {cb_warren_guide} {in_list}.
background: Her three children attended Warren schools from kindergarten through 12th grade and have graduated; age 55 {cb_warren_guide}.
First elected in 2014; now board president {cb_warren_guide}. WFYI reported in 2022 that she was a member of the Indiana School Boards Association {cb_warren_2022}.
path_to_ballot: Listed on the state candidate list as Nonpartisan {in_list}.

items: Called inadequate state funding the most pressing issue and would advocate with legislators and other districts for "a more equitable funding formula" {cb_warren_guide}.
Said any request for more money, such as a referendum, should rest on "a demonstrated need and a clear plan" {cb_warren_guide}.
Would put classroom instruction, student support services and competitive teacher pay first, and look for efficiencies {cb_warren_guide}.

Cited improved IREAD results (more than 83% of third graders passing) and said the focus is now ILEARN math; supports evidence-based instruction, teacher professional development and monitoring of achievement data {cb_warren_guide}.
Said low teacher pay makes recruiting and keeping educators difficult, and wants to keep salaries as competitive as possible {cb_warren_guide}.
Wants regular updates on board decisions and openness with residents about the district's financial challenges {cb_warren_guide}.

on_incumbent: Is a current board member and president. She credits the district with steady achievement gains over the past three years and supports the planned fifth-grade transition, including leadership opportunities for fifth graders {cb_warren_guide}.
plans: Wants to work with legislators and other districts on state funding, and to plan staffing, space and programming for the fifth-grade move {cb_warren_guide}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or campaign finance figures were found in reviewed sources {cb_warren_guide}.
gaps: No campaign website or social media page was found.
No record of her individual board votes was reviewed.
Marion County Election Board campaign finance filings were not reviewed; fundraising is unknown.
